market_story.title: The Fed is keeping rates high
market_story.body: USD and CAD remain supported, while EUR, JPY, and NZD stay under pressure.
drivers: USD: The Fed is keeping rates high
EUR: The ECB is moving toward rate cuts
JPY: Yen waiting for a market trigger

USD.label: Supported
USD.headline: The Fed is keeping rates high
reasons: The Fed is keeping rates high and has no plans to cut
The dollar remains the world's most-used currency
USD.insight: Higher rates keep money flowing into the dollar

EUR.label: Weak
EUR.headline: The ECB is moving toward rate cuts
reasons: The ECB is becoming more open to rate cuts
The economic data has been consistently weak
Slow growth in Germany is a persistent drag
EUR.insight: Rate cuts ahead are taking the shine off the euro

GBP.label: Neutral
GBP.headline: The BOE is watching and waiting
reasons: The BOE is waiting for clearer economic data
High inflation is limiting the BOE's room to act
GBP.insight: The pound is caught between growth worries and inflation

JPY.label: Weak
JPY.headline: Yen waiting for a market trigger
reasons: The yen is highly sensitive to sudden mood changes
The BOJ is actively cutting rates
JPY.insight: A sudden shift in mood could move the yen fast

CHF.label: Neutral
CHF.headline: Franc steady with no strong catalyst
reasons: Swiss stability is steady in the background
No single driver stands out right now
CHF.insight: Calm markets keep the franc in a holding pattern

CAD.label: Supported
CAD.headline: The BOC isn't ready to cut yet
reasons: Oil prices and US economic health are the key drivers
The BOC wants to see more progress before cutting rates
CAD.insight: Oil prices often move before CAD does

AUD.label: Neutral
AUD.headline: The RBA is watching and waiting
reasons: Commodity prices and China remain the key factors
No single driver stands out right now
AUD.insight: The next big move will likely come from outside Australia

NZD.label: Weak
NZD.headline: The RBNZ is moving toward rate cuts
reasons: Global trade conditions matter more than local data
The RBNZ is becoming more open to rate cuts
NZD.insight: Global sentiment is the dominant driver here
